llm.summary: This skill needs Review because it can handle wallet private keys, send live blockchain transactions, cache auth tokens, run background auto-replies, and has an overbroad authenticated API helper.

dimensions.detail: The main SKILL.md does disclose Provider lifecycle workflows and on-chain transaction helpers, but the public description emphasizes inspection, auto-reply, reads, and dispute checks; the actual artifacts include minting agents, staking USDC, delivery settlement, generic REST mutations, and raw transaction broadcast.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The docs ask for user confirmation before value-bearing transactions, but scripts/aacp-tx.mjs does not enforce confirmation and accepts arbitrary target/calldata/value tx-intents. scripts/aacp-api.mjs also accepts absolute URLs while attaching cached bearer tokens by default.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package is a Node-based skill made of markdown docs and local .mjs helper scripts, with no evidence of install-time execution or package-install hooks in the reviewed artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill asks users to supply WALLET_KEY, LLM API keys, cached session/runtime tokens, file uploads, and RPC/network access. These are partly purpose-aligned but high-impact for a marketplace and wallet automation skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The autoreply flow intentionally self-detaches a background worker that polls inbox messages and posts replies until stopped. It is documented and has a stop command, but it grants ongoing business-message authority outside the foreground session.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to let the skill operate Termix Provider workflows with wallet-level authority. Use a dedicated low-balance wallet, avoid pasting a primary private key into chat or shell history, prefer dry-run before any transaction, verify every contract address and amount, do not pass full external URLs to the authenticated API helper, and stop the autoreply worker when it is no longer needed.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] expected: Provider lifecycle and on-chain registration/staking capabilities are present in SKILL.md and workflow docs, so they are not hidden, but they are broader than the short skill description implies.
[SDI-2] expected: Private-key signing and transaction broadcast support is real and purpose-aligned for the documented Provider workflows, but the executor is generic and lacks an enforced confirmation or allowlist.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The authenticated API helper's absolute-URL behavior is not needed for Termix platform workflows and can send bearer tokens to non-Termix URLs.
[SDI-2] expected: Inbox text is sent to the configured OpenAI-compatible LLM during autoreply; the behavior is documented, but users should treat buyer messages as shared with that LLM provider.
[SDI-2] expected: The detached autoreply worker is an intended feature and is documented with pid/log/stop controls, but it is still persistent automated posting authority.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The transaction script comment says the printed plan lets an operator or LLM confirm before broadcast, but the code continues automatically unless --dry-run is used.
[SQP-2] expected: The docs repeatedly use WALLET_KEY and some upload/public URL workflows; these are expected for wallet and evidence operations, but the safety guidance is incomplete for raw private keys, public artifacts, and sensitive credentials.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Several legacy AACPCore docs contain older high-risk flows, but SKILL.md explicitly marks them as not applicable to dev-v2 and says not to load them for current workflows, so those findings are downgraded rather than treated as active runtime scope.
